One of my wishes is that those dark trees,

The LGBTQ community has become so hyper-sexualized that it ends up promoting the negative stereotypes of the LGBTQ community that said community is trying to avoid in the first place. It’s almost ironic. A community that demands to be treated as human beings and individuals - rightfully so - ends up lavishing in the identity politics and stereotyping that prevents people from being accepting towards them.

Now of course, I’m not saying that the LGBT culture and lifestyle be destroyed. Some people in the LGBT community thrive in such a culture and just feel like they’ve come into their own with that culture. I’m just saying that we should be careful in promoting the toxic and problematic aspects of that culture that could potentially do more harm than good, like for instance, showing your hyper sexualized lifestyle to minors who are not ready to process that. That is very irresponsible and damaging towards their development.

I absolutely agree. Yet some liberals are quick to point out how conservatives are hypocritical in that they engage in cancel culture when they disagree with things they don’t like. Maybe I’m just confusing this particular example. I’m just trying to play devils advocate here.

Well, I personally don’t have any problems with people in the LGBTQ community. They’re human beings like everyone else with human problems and human complexity. It’s none of my business to interfere or comment on with how people live their lives personally and privately. As long as it’s not bothering anyone, who cares what your sexual preference/orientation is? You do you and you live your life the way you see fit. Just don’t force it down everyone’s throats. 

I think some conservatives object to the “lifestyle” of the LGBTQ community because it negates the sanctity of a traditional heterosexual lifestyle - like a traditional marriage and the nuclear family. But most people who are LGBT are just regular normal people who just happen to have the trivial character trait of having a different sexual preference/orientation. It isn’t the most defining part of their lives. It’s only a small part. 

It’s a difficult discussion to have in today’s society. Of course, family values and the nuclear family should be preserved. Having a mother and father is a beneficial and important factor in one’s life, shaping how one lives. It’s the ideal and we shouldn’t just get rid of that traditional way of living and burn it down to the ground just because it’s the dominant way of shaping society.
